sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next word of a line ('die before your ___'). Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason out 'time' over 'harvest' or 'wedding'. It is a wording guess, not a meaning question.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the wording of verse 21 ('your ___ cursing you'). Card 12 never mentions a servant, so the baker can only guess among servant, neighbor and brother.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: Card 8 already asked who escapes the snare and revealed that only the man who pleases God does. Card 9 re-asks the same fact from the other half of verse 26 ('the sinner is ensnared'). The wording of card 8, 'one kind of man escapes', also gives card 9's answer away.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.
